comparator.sourceNotes: TU Delft's current programme page, checked 2026-10-03, describes a three-year bachelor structured around people, organisations and technology, with design projects integrating those domains. Its linked official 2026-2027 curriculum image accounts for the complete 180 EC: four 30-EC semesters of compulsory design projects and supporting courses, a 30-EC minor, and a final 30-EC semester comprising 15 EC of electives and a 15-EC bachelor final design project. The components below reproduce every named block and exact credit value from that curriculum.

programmes.label: Bachelor Industrial Design Engineering at Delft University of Technology

exception.reason: TU Delft's bachelor is a cumulative design education built around five substantial design projects, including a 15-EC bachelor final project, and a compulsory progression through design methods and research, human-centred design, digital interfaces, intelligent products, product engineering, sustainability, futures and organisational value. UCR offers one strong consumer-product-design course and useful adjacent courses in entrepreneurship, consumer research, psychology, data, software, robotics, sustainability and creative communication. It does not offer the repeated studio/project spine, industrial-design visualisation and form-giving sequence, ergonomics and usability sequence, materials and manufacturing progression, physical and digital prototyping sequence, or integrated product-engineering formation needed to represent Industrial Design Engineering. A 24-course UCR response would therefore be a liberal-arts programme with one product-design experience and several adjacent subjects, not a defensible disciplinary comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The official 2026-2027 curriculum accounts for all 180 EC. Years one and two each contain two 10-EC design projects supported by compulsory people, organisation, technology, research, values, data, sustainability and futures courses. Year three consists of a 30-EC minor followed by three 5-EC electives and the 15-EC Design Project 5 bachelor final project. TU Delft's programme page explains that students learn to design from the user's perspective, study aesthetics, interaction and usability, and develop knowledge of mechanics, materials, production methods, digital products and services, organisational value and societal, economic and environmental effects. Those domains are repeatedly integrated in design projects rather than sampled as separate electives.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design is the closest substantive match: students investigate customer needs, develop a product concept and fabrication method, build a prototype, model quantitatively, and assess sustainability, costs and intellectual property. BENGATE101 Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, BENENTR211 Marketing & Consumer Engagement, BENENTR212 Strategy & Digital Transformation, BENENTR311 Market Research and BENLEAD311 Psychology of Organizations & Leadership support customer, organisation and innovation perspectives. HCBPSYC111 Social Psychology and HCBCOGN212 Perception & Action provide adjacent human-behaviour evidence. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming, DISCOMP213 Software Development, DISDATA111 Introduction to Data Science, DISDATA212 Image Processing & Computer Vision and DISDATA312 Robotics provide digital and computational capabilities. ENSDELT111 Building with Nature, ENSDELT211 Living with Water, ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design and MCCCOMM312 Creative Communication Laboratory add project, sustainability and creative contexts. The workbook nevertheless contains no industrial-design studio sequence, drawing or design-visualisation progression, form and aesthetics studio, ergonomics/usability laboratory, materials and manufacturing course sequence, CAD or physical prototyping sequence, interaction-design sequence, integrated product-engineering curriculum, or capstone industrial-design studio. Several adjacent courses cannot substitute for five compulsory design projects and their cumulative technical and human-centred design formation.
